## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c87603a2a628344cbc4e1867280016f71707ca5e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md + none (no implementing file is in the diff; `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` on `origin/main` was read to judge the ADR, not reviewed)

Inputs: card #32674 (body, triage, claim, os-dev-report), PR #33460 (body, one-file list, net diff against `main` at merge base `ba35dfd7`), and the 50 check-runs on the head. `main` has since moved to `0c2aeb96`; no commit after the merge base touches the ADR or the gate, so the gate read on `origin/main` is the gate the amendment describes. Check-runs at review time: 15 success, 26 skipped, 9 in progress (Test Core 1/8, Type Check x4, Lint x4), none failed. The in-progress runs have to go green before landing; this record does not stand in for them.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: unchanged. The diff touches no gate, schema or code. The ADR's documented category set, read with the gate's own `documentedCategories` pattern (`adr-0087\s*:\s*not-required\s*\(\s*([a-z-]+)`) on base and head, is the same six on both: `already-registered`, `no-migration-prescription`, `runtime-export-retired`, `runtime-interface-only`, `type-surface-only`, `unpublished`. That is exactly `CATEGORIES` on `main`, so `assertInputs`' VOCABULARY DRIFT check (both directions) cannot fire. The diff adds no marker example. Right.
- Public surface: none. `docs/adr/**` ships in no package. Right.
- Gate vocabulary: no category, marker spelling, signal name (`NARROWED_SIGNAL` = `metadata-protocol-narrowed`) or refusal text changed. Right.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` (label applied; Check Changeset is success). That matches a diff that publishes nothing. The PR body carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, both correct for a prose-only ADR amendment that narrows nothing an author writes. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- Dev deviation 1 (thread ran at the claim's default tier, while `dispatch-gates --tier` mandates contract-review tier for `docs/adr/**`): answered by this record, which is the owed review at tier.
- Dev deviations 2 and 3 (the signature is a prose line rather than an HTML comment; the commit carries a model-free trailer pair): process only, outside ④. Not escalated.
- Out-of-scope note (the Status block does not list this amendment; the 2026-10-12 table row at :1078 stays as measured): see ④ finding 4 for the Status block. The :1078 row is a dated measurement of #22875 under the gate as it stood then, and is correctly left alone.

### ④ Design judgment

`docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md`, against its first consumer `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` on `main`, sentence by sentence:

- "it is also refused outright, before its justification or its body is read": holds. In `scan()`, the `no-migration-prescription` plus `NARROWED_SIGNAL` check sits right after `CATEGORIES.includes` and before the 40-character `why` check and every prescription-detector read. This matches the gate header's own wording ("before its justification or its body is read").
- "on a changeset that declares `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, signal (5) of the breaking declaration": holds. `breakingDeclaration()` pushes `NARROWED_SIGNAL` only when `readMetadataProtocolLine` returns `kind === 'declared' && value === 'narrowed'`, which is signal (5) in its docblock.
- The reason sentence ("A narrowing refuses something an author used to write ... upgrade guide and `objectstack migrate meta`, both generated from the ledger ... before a save door, a publish or a boot refuses it; whether the fix is written as an arrow, a table or a sentence does not change that"): a faithful paraphrase of the refusal message in `scan()` and the header section "A declared narrowing owes the upgrade guide (#32601)".
- The prescription ("a `registered` semantic entry, one file under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/`, or a category resting on a checked fact when one is true: `already-registered`, `unpublished`, `runtime-interface-only`, `type-surface-only`, `runtime-export-retired`"): matches the refusal text (`MIGRATION_LEDGER_ENTRY_DIRS[0]` is `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic`). The open list is exactly the gate's: in `scan()` the refusal is keyed on `d.category === 'no-migration-prescription'` alone, so every other category stays open on a narrowing.
- "If the change refuses nothing an author could write, the `Metadata-protocol:` line is what is wrong, not the disposition": matches the refusal text's last line.
- Boundaries ("`added`, `semantic` and `none` keep the exemption, and a changeset already breaking at the branch point is inherited and never re-judged"): hold. Those three kinds push no signal. The `M`/`R` branch in `scan()` skips a changeset whose base-side text is already breaking by any signal, which is exactly "already breaking at the branch point".
- Table row note at :880 ("on a changeset declaring `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` it is refused before the body is read; see the vocabulary paragraph of the 2026-08-13 addendum"): correct. The measured text "refused — the body carries a FROM/TO block." is kept, and the pointer resolves to the heading "the changeset disposition vocabulary".
- No ruled sentence deleted: the word diff replaces only the closing `prescription;` with `prescription (` + insertion + `);`. The −6 lines are the same words re-wrapped, and the table row's measured text is intact. Amendments annotate.
- Citations: #32601 is the gate card (closed by PR #32649). Its body's "Seat decision (option A of the dev's three ...)" is the rule stated. PR #32649 merged at merge commit `a8c761fbe5ec06978f5e3582a35cf8be0c0503ae` on 2026-11-12, which is the amendment's date. All accurate. Seat decision A's own open list omits `runtime-export-retired`; the amendment follows the landed gate, which includes it. That is the right source to follow, and the gate dev flagged it on #32601.
- Style: `(**amended DATE**, #card ...: ...)` matches the ADR's existing inline amendments (e.g. :147, :562).

Findings:

1. nit. The ADR still says "the `no-migration-prescription` refusal" in the singular at :823 (D7, `runtime-interface-only` "also inherits" it), :881 (table, "inherits that same refusal"), :1001 (`type-surface-only` "the only category exempt from" it) and :1204 (`runtime-export-retired` "inherits" it). Each means the body-prescription refusal, and the gate inherits only that one. The category now has two refusals, though, and a reader who enters at D7 does not see that the narrowing refusal is not inherited. The amendment's explicit open list settles it, so there is no contract effect. Accepted deviation, or a follow-up card if the seat wants the four sentences qualified.
2. nit. The amendment's "declares" carries the gate's DECLARED-reading boundary unstated: a malformed or near-miss `Metadata-protocol:` line triggers nothing here. The gate header calls this a deliberate boundary pinned in the NP battery. There is no contract effect, because the level gate refuses such a line on the PR. Accepted deviation.
3. nit. "The fix is a `registered` semantic entry" mirrors the refusal's own prescription, but `registered` accepts any id that is new in the diff and resolves in `LEDGER_SOURCES`. The migration registry is generated from all three `MIGRATION_LEDGER_ENTRY_DIRS` (semantic, retired-keys, retired-defs), so a new retired-keys entry for a removed key also clears the gate. Prescriptive rather than exclusive, and it matches the gate's text. Accepted deviation.
4. nit. The Status block lists no amendment for this rule change. Precedent is mixed: inline amendments 2026-08-06 (#5837) and 2026-09-13 (#18003) are also absent from it, and the dated inline note plus the table pointer make the change findable. Accepted deviation, or a follow-up card if the maintainer wants the Status block exhaustive.

No must-fix and no should-fix: nits alone end the round.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:ADR-0087 处置一节与类别表行补记第二种拒绝：变更集声明 `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` 时,`no-migration-prescription` 也被拒(PR #32649 起门禁已如此),并写明原因、处方与仍开放的类别。只加注，不删已裁定的句子。
- 为什么改：门禁与它所依据的 ADR 文字不一致，作者照 ADR 写标记会撞上 ADR 没解释的拒绝(卡 #32674)。
- 风险与回滚：纯文档，不动门禁与类别词表(ADR 与 `CATEGORIES` 仍是同样六类)。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:ADR-0087 处置段落里带 2026-11-12 日期的插注，再看类别表那一行的注。
- 两分钟验证:`git diff origin/main -- docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md`。
- 需要你做的：受管面 Tier H(`docs/adr/**`),契约复审 PASS 评论 6884807805(Head-sha `c87603a2a628344cbc4e1867280016f71707ca5e`)已在案，请批准或直接合并。
- 席位意见：可以合。复审逐句对照 `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`:触发条件、在 `scan()` 中的顺序、处方、仍开放的类别与边界均成立;四处措辞小瑕疵记为接受的偏差。

## 席位核对

**Verdict: ACCEPT, held for the maintainer** · head `c87603a2a628344cbc4e1867280016f71707ca5e` · card #32674 · report 6884608125 · contract review 6884807805 (PASS on this head, CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER; Ruling-ref for the in-seat review: Leehom card cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XFhuiZmTH8VFgMmHRmpiGAb option A).

- **Shape:** draft → `main`, `Fixes #32674`. `docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md` (+19 / -6, the -6 is re-wrapping of the same words). `skip-changeset`. **GOVERNED**, Tier H (`docs/adr/**`). `Clause-②: no`; `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Contract:** the amendment states signal (5) from `breakingDeclaration()`, its place in `scan()`, the refusal's reason and its fix (`MIGRATION_LEDGER_ENTRY_DIRS[0]`), the open categories (equal to the gate's) and the boundaries, all as the merged gate (`a8c761fb`) makes them. The ADR's documented categories still equal `CATEGORIES`; `assertInputs` cannot fire.
- **Gates:** 25 derived, 25 exit 0 (ADR-0087 self-test and `--base` run included). Check-runs on the head all concluded, none failing.
- **Accepted deviations (review nits):** N1, four later places (D7 and three more) say "the `no-migration-prescription` refusal" in the singular, meaning the body-prescription one; the amendment's explicit open list settles the reading. N2, "declares" leaves out that a malformed `Metadata-protocol:` line triggers nothing. N3, "the fix is a `registered` semantic entry" is a recommendation; any `LEDGER_SOURCES` id passes. N4, the Status block does not list the amendment (precedent mixed).
- **Process:** the thread ran at the default tier, met by this in-seat review.
- **Landing:** Tier H. The seat does not flip this PR ready or enqueue it. It needs the maintainer's merge, or an authorised APPROVED review after which the seat lands it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c87603a2a628344cbc4e1867280016f71707ca5e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md + none (no implementing file is in the diff; `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, `packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry.ts` and the entry directories on `main` were read to judge the ADR, never reviewed)

At-tier re-review, judged from the tree. Inputs: card #32674 (body and all four comments), PR #33460 (body, one-file list, net diff against `main` from merge base `ba35dfd7`), and the check-runs on the head. `main` is now `8e63ed87`; no commit between the merge base and it touches the ADR or the gate, so the gate read on `main` is the gate the amendment describes. Check-runs on the head: every run completed, conclusions are success or skipped only, none failed or cancelled (Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test Core, Type Check all success).

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: unchanged. One prose file; no gate, schema or code in the diff. The diff adds no `adr-0087: not-required (CATEGORY` marker example, so the set `documentedCategories` reads off the ADR is the same six on base and head and equals `CATEGORIES` on `main` (`unpublished`, `already-registered`, `no-migration-prescription`, `runtime-interface-only`, `type-surface-only`, `runtime-export-retired`). `assertInputs`' VOCABULARY DRIFT check cannot fire in either direction. Right.
- Public surface: none. `docs/adr/**` ships in no package. Right.
- Ruled text: the word diff removes exactly one token, the closing `prescription;`, replaced by `prescription (` + the insertion + `);`. The other removed lines are the same words re-wrapped, and the table row keeps its measured sentence whole. Nothing ruled is deleted or re-graded. Right.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` label, Check Changeset success: matches a diff that publishes nothing. PR body carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; both are correct for an ADR annotation that changes no accept set and nothing an author writes. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- Dev deviation 1 (the thread ran at the claim's default tier while `dispatch-gates --tier` reads MANDATORY contract-review tier for `docs/adr/**`): answered by this record, the owed review at tier.
- Dev deviations 2 and 3 (prose signature line instead of an HTML comment; model-free commit trailer pair): process only, no contract face. Not escalated.
- Dev out-of-scope note (Status block not extended; the 2026-10-12 table row at :1078 left as measured): the :1078 row is a dated measurement of #22875 under the gate of its day and is correctly untouched; the Status block is finding 4 below.
- Earlier record 6884807805 (served off-tier; not used as evidence): it raised four nits and no must-fix or should-fix, so there is no fix owed on this head. Judged independently, I confirm all four (they are findings 1 to 4 below) and reject none. Its per-sentence readings of `scan()` and `breakingDeclaration()` match what the tree says. I add two nits it did not raise (5 and 6).

### ④ Design judgment

`docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md`, against its first consumer, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` on `main`, and against the decision it records (#32601, seat decision A; PR #32649 merged 2026-11-12 as `a8c761fbe5ec06978f5e3582a35cf8be0c0503ae`).

Sentence by sentence (:765 to :778):

- "also refused outright, before its justification or its body is read": holds. In `scan()` the check `d.category === 'no-migration-prescription' && decl.signals.includes(NARROWED_SIGNAL)` sits directly after the `CATEGORIES.includes` refusal and before the 40-character `why` check and before any `findMigrationPrescription` read. Same words as the gate's header section "A declared narrowing owes the upgrade guide (#32601)".
- "on a changeset that declares `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, signal (5) of the breaking declaration": holds. `breakingDeclaration()` pushes `NARROWED_SIGNAL` only for `kind.kind === 'declared'` with value `narrowed`, read from the changeset body by the imported `readMetadataProtocolLine`; that is item 5 of its docblock.
- The reason sentences (a narrowing refuses something an author used to write; the upgrade guide and `objectstack migrate meta`, generated from the ledger, are where an upgrading author learns it; arrow, table or sentence does not change that): a faithful restatement of the refusal message and the header section. No claim beyond them.
- "The fix is a `registered` semantic entry, one file under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/`": that path is `MIGRATION_LEDGER_ENTRY_DIRS[0]`, the directory the refusal text and the #32601 Ask both name. The same ADR paragraph, two lines up, already states the real `registered` rule (ids that resolve and are new in the diff), so the accept rule is not misstated; see finding 3.
- "or a category resting on a checked fact when one is true: `already-registered`, `unpublished`, `runtime-interface-only`, `type-surface-only`, `runtime-export-retired`": exactly the gate's open set. The refusal is keyed on the one category, so the other five stay open on a narrowing, each under its own re-checked predicate. Seat decision A's text lists four; the gate as landed adds `runtime-export-retired`, and the ADR rightly follows the landed gate.
- "If the change refuses nothing an author could write, the `Metadata-protocol:` line is what is wrong, not the disposition": the refusal message's last sentence.
- "`added`, `semantic` and `none` keep the exemption": holds; none of the three pushes a signal, and the category then falls through to the ordinary body check.
- "a changeset already breaking at the branch point is inherited and never re-judged": holds; the `M` / `R` branch reads the base-side text and skips the file when `breakingDeclaration` is already true there, before any disposition is read.

Table row (:880): the measured sentence stays; the note says the category is refused before the body is read on a declared narrowing and points to "the vocabulary paragraph of the 2026-08-13 addendum", which resolves to the heading at :732 ("the changeset disposition vocabulary, and its fifth category"). Correct, and it does not re-grade the #12104 measurement.

Attempts to break it, none of which lands:

- A second, contradicting statement of the rule elsewhere in the ADR: every other `no-migration-prescription` mention (:800, :823, :912, :1001, :1078, :1083, :1204, :1224, :1249) is about the body-prescription refusal or a dated measurement; none says the category is open to a narrowing.
- A narrowing declared by the direction arm alone (signal (4), no `narrowed` kind): the gate does not refuse it, and the ADR does not say it does; the amendment is worded on the kind, not on narrowing in general.
- Citation and date: #32601 is closed by PR #32649, whose merge commit and merge date are the ones cited; the inline `(**amended DATE**, #card ...)` form matches :147 and :562.
- Mechanical gates on the changed file (adr links, anchors, symbol anchors, index, doc authoring): all inside green check-runs on the head. No link, anchor or marker example was added.

Findings (all nits; none affects correctness or the contract):

1. nit. :823 (D7), :881, :1001 (D8) and :1204 (D9) still say "the `no-migration-prescription` refusal" in the singular. Each means the body-prescription refusal, which is the only one those categories inherit or are exempt from; the amendment's explicit open list settles the reading. Accepted deviation, or a follow-up card to qualify the four sentences.
2. nit. "declares" leaves the DECLARED-reading boundary unstated: a malformed or near-miss `Metadata-protocol:` line, or a changeset carrying no such line, triggers nothing in this gate (the level gate refuses a bad line on the PR). The gate header calls this deliberate and pins it in the NP battery. Accepted deviation.
3. nit. "The fix is a `registered` semantic entry" is the decision's and the refusal's own prescription, but narrower than what the gate admits: `registered` accepts any id new in the diff under either `LEDGER_SOURCES` registry, and the migration registry is built from all three entry directories (semantic, retired-keys, retired-defs). A removed key, the first shape `narrowed` names, is properly a retired-key entry. The paragraph's own `registered` sentence carries the true rule and an author following the ADR is never refused, so no contract effect. Accepted deviation.
4. nit. The Status block does not list this amendment. Precedent is mixed (the inline 2026-08-06 #5837 and 2026-09-13 #18003 amendments are not listed either), and this one records a seat decision under an existing gate, not a maintainer ruling. Accepted deviation, or a follow-up card if the maintainer wants the block exhaustive.
5. nit (new). "signal (5) of the breaking declaration" and the `Metadata-protocol:` line itself are defined nowhere in the ADR; both live in the gate's `breakingDeclaration` docblock (ruling A, #25105). The paragraph ends by pointing at the gate file, so the reference resolves one hop away. Accepted deviation.
6. nit (new). The amendment is a thirteen-line, seven-sentence parenthesis inside one item of a semicolon list, so the list's remaining items (`runtime-interface-only`, `type-surface-only`, `runtime-export-retired`) now start mid-paragraph after it. It is the ADR's own inline-amendment form (:562) and reads correctly; a blockquote note under the paragraph would read easier. Prose only. Accepted deviation.

No must-fix and no should-fix: nits alone end the round.

## Correction: contract-review tier

The contract-review record(s) 6884807805 on this PR say `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, and the seat adopted them as "isolated sub-agent at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER". **That is wrong.** The seat launched the reviewing sub-agent without the tier, so it ran at the seat's own default tier, not at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The seat found this on its own audit. The review was still isolated and adversarial, and its findings stand as an off-tier review. They are not the at-tier record AGENTS.md and the in-seat review ruling require.

The seat re-runs the review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this PR's head and posts that record here. Until it does, this PR has no at-tier record.
